subject: Capacity bridge & staggered reservation options for Limnotech
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Solis <anna@limnotech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity bridge & staggered reservation options for Limnotech

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, attached is a compact set of reservation options that map to the three usage profiles you shared (pilot burst, steady inference, and scale-out training bursts). The goal here is to give you a low-friction on-ramp (a short-term capacity bridge) while protecting unit economics as you move to a committed plan.

Summary (high level):
- Bridge lane (0–8 weeks): short-term burstable pool on shared GPUs to support proof-of-concept traffic and early model tuning. Recommended: 4 x A100-equiv lanes with 1:6 oversubscription for cost efficiency.
- Committed baseline (weeks 9–26): minimum guaranteed pool to meet steady-state inference SLOs. Options below: 16, 32, or 48 GPUs (A100/RTX-class) with reserved throughput targets.
- Burst cushion (optional): a small reserved burst credit for training or sudden traffic spikes; bill only when consumed.

Key differentiators in the attached model: per-token cost with/without KV caching, expected 95th-pct latency at median context length, and a ramp schedule tied to milestones in your ML roadmap (POC completion, model freeze, full rollout).

Two things I need from you to finalize numbers:
1) Confirmation if you need H100-class performance for the training bursts or if A100/80GB is sufficient.
2) A target SLA latency number for inference p95 (e.g., 200ms target at 512 tokens) so we can size the minimum GPUs accordingly.

Attached: limnotech_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet shows per-week burn and latency assumptions) and proposed_contract_terms.pdf (straightforward reserved terms with a 3-month bridge clause).

Next step: I propose a 30-min follow-up next Tuesday to walk the spreadsheet and agree on Option A/B/C. Does 10:30am PT work?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184
Redwood Inference

From: Anna Solis <anna@limnotech.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@limnotech.com
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity bridge & staggered reservation options for Limnotech

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear breakdown. A few quick clarifications before we lock a time: 

- GPU class: For now our inference workload will run on A100-class; the training bursts may need H100 starting Q4 depending on model complexity. Can you include an add-on price delta for H100 equivalent capacity?
- SLA / latency: Our product team is targeting p95 <= 250ms at 256 tokens for the initial rollout. We can re-evaluate for longer contexts in phase 2.
- SOC 2 & compliance: procurement asks for a short SOC 2 excerpt and retention policy summary we can include with our security review.
- PoC window: We'd like a 3-week POC with a small set of test traffic routed to Redwood so we can validate latency under our real payloads. Any concerns on the Redwood side?

Also please include a one-line explanation of how the bridge lane is billed vs the committed baseline (e.g., prorated credits, overage rates). If possible, can you attach an example invoice cadence?

I can do Tuesday at 10:30am PT. Anna

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Solis <anna@limnotech.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, procurement@limnotech.com
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity bridge & staggered reservation options for Limnotech

Anna — thanks for the clear list. A few notes and answers inline.

> GPU class: For now our inference workload will run on A100-class; the training bursts may need H100 starting Q4 depending on model complexity. Can you include an add-on price delta for H100 equivalent capacity?

Yes — we included an H100 uplift option in the spreadsheet (tab: "HW-deltas"). Roughly +28% unit cost for H100 burst minutes; we can also offer a reserved H100 tranche at a lower uplift if you want to lock a small training lane in advance.

> SLA / latency: Our product team is targeting p95 <= 250ms at 256 tokens for the initial rollout.

Good target — our sizing table maps that latency to a minimum baseline of 16 GPUs with eager KV caching and a ~8ms per-token kernel on A100. If you want stricter p95 we can recommend 32 GPUs. See spreadsheet rows 18–24 for the simulated latency curves.

> SOC 2 & compliance: procurement asks for a short SOC 2 excerpt and retention policy summary we can include with our security review.

Attached here is a short snippet of our compliance summary for procurement. (Attachment: redwood_soc2_excerpt.pdf)

> PoC window: We'd like a 3-week POC with a small set of test traffic routed to Redwood so we can validate latency under our real payloads. Any concerns on the Redwood side?

No concerns — the proposed bridge lane is designed for exactly that. Operational notes:
- Onboarding takes ~48 hours once we receive an API key and a test model bundle.
- We’ll provision the bridge pool (4 A100 lanes) and enable KV caching with your prefix sets.
- Telemetry will be shared via a temp dashboard (link below) and we’ll add your engineering contacts to the workspace.

Billing & example cadence:
- Bridge lane is billed as a short-term reservation at a discounted hourly rate (shown in the spreadsheet) plus metered overage if burst > provisioned hours.
- Committed baseline is a monthly reservation invoice with monthly reporting; unused committed hours are credited at the end of each billing quarter (see Terms, section 3).
- Example invoice cadence: initial month contains bridge charges pro-rated + first monthly reservation invoice; subsequent bills follow monthly.

Next steps and materials we attached/linked:
- limnotech_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (your copy with H100 deltas)
- proposed_contract_terms.pdf (clean terms)
- redwood_soc2_excerpt.pdf (procurement requested snippet)
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleShare/limnotech-capacity
- DocuSign (placeholder for signature): https://www.docusign.com/contract/LIM-2027-3472

Vanessa — we’ll run the 30-min walkthrough on Tuesday at 10:30am PT as planned. I’ll drop in a short meeting invite.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

(On behalf of Marcus Lin — cc'd)
